Image 1 = real photos of the flashlight: front, back, a close-up of its logo, its USB-A port, and its end cap pulled off showing the USB-C port; Image 2 = a real photo of the flashlight standing upright with its carabiner clip on top: its true slim proportions and the order of its parts; Image 3 = her real hand: skin tone, nails, rings and bracelets; Image 4 = an approved photo from this same series: match its hand, skin, French-tip nails, rings and bracelets exactly; Image 5 = an approved photo of the same campsite from this series: match its tent, picnic table, pine trees, mountains, colours and how dark the scene is.

Make one photo (shot S7 of a 9-photo video series). SIZE FIRST: the flashlight is 15.7 cm long including its clip and 2.95 cm square, about 5 times as long as it is wide, 90 g. It is about as long as a phone and as wide as two fingers. Slim, never stubby, never a big torch.

SCENE: Top-down close-up: an open plain dark-blue zip pouch on the picnic table with bandages, a small water bottle and a roll of tape inside. Her hand grips the flashlight by its dark metal end cap and is lowering it into the pouch, light off, the orange button visible. The pouch has no cross, no logo and no writing.

HER HAND (the only person in the photo): exactly the hand in the hand image: medium-brown skin, slim fingers, natural pink nails with crisp white French tips, a silver crown-shaped stack ring, a thin gold solitaire ring and a blue silicone band, a chunky gold watch-link bracelet and a thin gold chain with small pearls and a gold leaf charm on the wrist. The hand enters from the edge of the frame with the whole wrist visible; the fingers truly grip what they hold.

THE FLASHLIGHT must match the real photos exactly, part for part and colour for colour: a slim square bar with rounded corners, and its parts in this order from the clip end: a light blue-grey plastic carabiner clip with a thin silver wire gate; the light blue-grey matte body with a long rounded-rectangle frosted pale light panel; then ONE square orange button with an embossed power symbol; then a darker grey brushed-metal end cap (about a quarter of the length) whose tip is the lens: a rounded-square dark grey bezel around a clear domed zoom lens with a small square LED chip in its centre (no silver reflector). The only print on it: on the front of the dark end cap a white shark logo with the words SMILING SHARK in white bold letters, exactly as in the logo close-up, letter for letter; on the back of the cap a few lines of tiny white spec text; on the back of the body one small round hole near the clip. No other text, no stickers, no extra buttons, no screen, no second light. Only one flashlight in the photo.

PLACE: one campsite in a pine forest at blue hour, just after sunset: the dusk sky is darkened closer to night, a deep navy blue with only a faint pale glow at the horizon, while the campsite stays clearly visible: tent, table, ground and trees easy to see, true neutral colours, no orange, yellow or golden cast. A sage-green dome tent, a weathered wooden picnic table, pine trees and distant mountains.

Real photo taken on a phone, casual and realistic, like a real person took it. Vertical 9:16. No text, no captions, no watermark, no other logos or brand names anywhere, no lens flare, no sparkles, no light streaks.

LIGHT: the scene is dim like the approved campsite photo, the dusk sky darkened closer to night, so the flashlight's own light glows clearly and is the brightest thing in the photo, while the campsite stays visible.

FIX: the flashlight in her hand is the light blue-grey square bar from images 1 and 2, never a black or round torch: blue-grey body, frosted light panel, square orange button, dark grey end cap with SMILING SHARK, carabiner clip on the other end, all visible as she lowers it into the pouch.
